lessons.title: Notice the small costs
lessons.reading: Practice example: Jo buys a £3 snack on five days. That adds up to £15. These are invented amounts, not a recommended spending limit. Small purchases can be easy to forget. Writing them down can help explain where your money went. You decide which purchases matter to you. A spending record is information, not a reason to feel guilty.

lessons.title: Do a five-minute money check
lessons.description: Build a simple habit for reviewing your plan.
lessons.reading: Practice example: Lee has £100 available and a known £40 payment due before more money arrives. Reserving that payment leaves £60 for other costs. A short check can include your available balance, payments still to come and any spending you have not yet recorded. Avoid counting the same money twice. If a figure does not look right, check the details before changing your plan. You can make notes and ask someone you trust to help you understand them.
